text:
ophelia-infra: FYI, just noticed a spike of gpu node join failures in ap-south after the new default-deny FW roll. Keystore egress is being blocked for worker subnets. 
ophelia-infra: Paste from node bootstrap logs:
```
2026-03-21T09:12:34Z ERROR keystore.Decrypt AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/node-join-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456:key/abcd
node join failed: instance=ip-10-0-5-21, err="keystore decrypt failed: AccessDenied"
```
michael-sre: Can we confirm whether the FW change also touched NAT/privnet routes? If nodes can't reach keystore endpoint (privnet-host:443) they'll never bootstrap. Quick mitigation: allow egress from worker-subnet SG to keystore host, port 443.
anya-platform: If we fall back to other regions or create on-demand pools we'll blow the Q1 infra forecast. We already have warm pools in eu-west but cross-region failovers will hit costs and latency. Estimate +$1.5k/day if we can't bring ap-south nodes up.
kai-security: That firewall tighten was deliberate to close an audit gap where keystore had overly broad access. We need an exception process; temporary SG exceptions are acceptable but must be timeboxed and logged with an audit ticket. Who can propose subnets and duration?
lucy-ops: Repro: nodes in worker-subnet-a and worker-subnet-b show repeated 403 Decrypt errors. NAT gateway flow logs show CONNECT to privnet-host getting RST. Looks like security group egress denies, not NAT capacity.
devon-bot: action: canary-rollback request queued -> rollback-fw-rule id fw-2026-ap-south-37 at 09:25 (manual approval required)
michael-sre: I'll open a minimal SG rule (allow worker-subnets -> privnet-host:443) with tag "keystore-temp-exception" and TTL 1h. Will also add an audit entry and comment the associated PR. Please ack.
kai-security: Ack. I need the exact subnet IDs and the justification in the audit ticket. TTL 1h is fine, but no open-ended exceptions. Also capture keystore access logs while exception active.
ophelia-infra: Subnets: subnet-0a1b2c3d, subnet-0d3c2b1a. Justification: nodes failing to decrypt ephemeral keys on boot, causing capacity shortage. Creating audit ticket INFRA-9487 and linking this thread.
michael-sre: Command I ran: ```aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-worker-egress --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/16 --description "keystore-temp-exception INFRA-9487 TTL=1h"```
devon-bot: deploybot: SG rule created sg-r-87f4, TTL annotation set, audit ticket INFRA-9487 updated.
jorge-cost: Tagging note: if we keep this open >1h and fallback to on-demand instances, cost projection goes up ~+$2k/day in ap-south until reserved capacity fills. Please escalate if we need extended window.
lucy-ops: Nodes are now starting to register, seeing k8s node join events at 09:30. Warm pool backfilling initiated.
kai-security: I'll review the keystore policy next. If this pattern repeats we need a KMS key policy change that scopes decrypt to the node join role and adds conditions, rather than broad network exceptions.
ophelia-infra: Agreed. Immediate status: capacity degraded for ~18 minutes, nodes backfilling, temporary SG exception in place for 1h. Follow-ups: (1) kai to propose KMS keypolicy update, (2) ops to add runbook step for FW->keystore interactions, (3) cost to model fallback exposure.
anya-platform: I'll update the incident runbook and add the cross-region failover cost matrix.
jorge-cost: Filing a quick cost alert for ap-south GPU on-demand usage if it exceeds baseline by 10% over next 24h.
ophelia-infra: Closing loop: thanks all. We'll snapshot keystore audit logs and attach to INFRA-9487. If anyone sees reoccurrence ping me. :thumbsup:
